claim: TASK-020 cuts Designer, design-session workflow, entry prompts, and deferred bootstrap to the seven current source-bound Design package operations.
evidence: Designer declares exactly create_design_session, read_design_session, revise_design_session, publish_design_checkpoint, derive_delivery_contract, validate_delivery_contract, and admit_delivery_change as its Kanban grants.
The workflow creates once, resumes through verified read, revises complete authored bytes by expected package ID, retains returned identity, and forbids direct package writes or local hashing.
Checkpoint, derive, validate, challenge/baseline evidence, approval, and admission are bound to one unchanged package identity with stale CAS routed to read and reconciliation.
Both prompts use the same package workflow and contain no retired list/show/validate/admit change API.
The global deferred query enumerates the current 23 Delivery operation names and no retired job, semantic-update, reviewer-arbitration, or liveness operation.
Structural validators, exact grant-to-registry comparison, 36 assembled server tests, 10 applicable ecosystem tests, semantic absence checks, lint, and diagnostics pass.
The only full-ecosystem failure is the pre-existing TargetAppContext import explicitly owned by TASK-017; independent review found no TASK-020 defect or exclusion violation.
